_comment: Add a _ before an option name to comment it out and it wont be added to the apworld
Using 'goal' as the name of an option let you override some of the generated goal parameters
goal.description: How to End your Randomized playthrough.

filler_traps._comment: Using values here let you set a 'recommended' filler_trap percentage or even a default percentage

description: When enabled, add progressive weapons going from rank D to A. E is available from start.
In this Manual, Tomes are split into their types instead of having a single Progressive Tome encompassing all of them, they're split into Fire, Wind, Thunder and Dark.
The Water Tome is just called 'Water Tome Rank A' as there is only one in the game.
All these items are considered as Useful.
When enabled, will add one of each weapon into the multiworld.
Rank A, B and C Weapons are considered as Useful.
Rank D and E Weapons are considered as Filler.
Beast and Dragonstones are considered as Progression. Their upgraded variants are considered useful however.
If 'Progressive_Weapons' is enabled, will add an additional Progressive Weapon of each type which will be required before a Character/Class is in logic.
If 'All_Weapons' is enabled, will also include every Rank E weapon in the pool.
Bronze Weapons will be considered as Progression for various Classes.
Only the Fire Tome will be labeled as Progression for Tome Classes.
Only the Heal Staff will be labeled as Progression for Staff Classes.
All other E Rank Weapons are considered as Filler Items.
When enabled, will randomize an item into the multiworld for each class restricting you from using them before found.
Base Only: Adds one of each Base Class as an item into the item pool.
Promoted Only: Adds one of each Promoted Class as an item into the item pool.
Base and Promoted: Adds both Base and Promoted Classes.
Character-Specific: Adds an item for each Character and their potential classes they can become, such as 'Robin's Tactician' and 'Chrom's Lord'.
Character-Specific Include Start Class: If enabled will also add an item of Each Class for Every Character's Starting Class they are when recruited.

NOTE: IF Character-Specific is enabled and 'Restrict ChildPair' is disabled, and then if you have Children enabled it will add one of each class for every child as the generator won't know which parents they will have ingame. This can add a lot of extra items.
Adds one of each Skill as an item into the item pool restricting you from using said skill until found.
These are considered as Filler and Useful Items.
The decision to decide what classifies as what was done entirely by personal taste.
Adds one of each item(exluding weapons, seals and dlc items) into the multiworld.
These are all considered as filler or useful items.
This option adds the Master and Second Seal into the multiworld.
Normal: A single Master and Second Seal will be added into the Multiworld.
Character-Specific: A Master and Second Seal for each character will be added into the multiworld, preventing you from promoting and reclassing that specific character until found.
These are considered as progression items and will be required before you can promote or reclass your characters.
When enabled will add an item for each Weapon Type as a Weapon License into the multiworld called 'Sword Weapon License', 'Staff Weapon License', 'Dragonstone Weapon License' and so forth.
The weapon types are: Swords, Lances, Axes, Bows, Tomes, Staves, Beaststone and Dragonstone.
The intention is that you cannot use any weapons before its license is found.
These are considered as Progression Items.
When enabled will add four of each item for each Character into the multiworld called 'Robin's Support Rank', 'Chrom's Support Rank' and so forth.
The intention is that you cannot progress through the support ranks without them. In the example above you would need both of them to get Chrom and Robin to reach C Rank Support.
You can manually restrain yourself from triggering the support rank upgrade.
1 is required for C, 2 is required for B, 3 is required for A and 4 are required for S. If a unit pair cannot have S Rank, just treat the fourth as filler.
These are considered as Progression Items.
When enabled will add five items for each category of Forging you can do to a weapon.
They're called 'Forging Might', 'Forging Hit' and 'Forging Critical'
The intention is that you cannot forge past the amount you have in a particular category when forging weapons!
These are considered as Useful Items.
When enabled every Paralogue(Side Story in EU) will be included as locations.
When enabled every Paralogue(Side Story in EU) will require an item of its name before it is accessible.
Does nothing if 'Enable_Paralogues' is disabled.
When enabled every Paralogue(Side Story in EU) will require a 'Progressive Paralogue Chapter' of the same amount of its number before it is accessible.
Does nothing if 'Restrict_Paralogues' is disabled.
When enabled every Child Character will be added into the pool.
To get the children's chapter in logic if Paralogues is enabled, you just need their mother and any father capable of marrying them.
Children will not be enabled if you have the Mad King as your goal.
When enabled, will balance options around Robin (Avatar) being male.
If disabled, will balance options around Robin (Avatar) being female.
Mainly used to decide which pairings to use in 'Restrict_ChildPairs'.
One item for each child which randomly decides their parents will be added into the pool named 'MotherName x FatherName'.
If using Paralogues, children won't be accessible until you've found the 'pairing item' in the world.
Chapter 11 will require a Chrom Pairing before it is accessible as Chrom forces a S Support level with his wife.
Does nothing if 'Enable_Children' is disabled.
When enabled, will include the extra Characters which only Robin can marry for their potential partners.
Those being the Future Children, Anna, Tiki, Say'ri, Flavia, Basilio and the Spotpass Characters.
This will add them progressively future_children > robin_exclusives > spotpass. If you enable spotpass then all of the others will also be included.
SpotPass Characters are not picked even if the setting is enabled if 'SpotPass_Characters' is disabled.
Does nothing if 'Restrict_ChildPairs' is disabled.
When enabled, will make Robin prioritize the 2nd Generation Units as their partner.
Those being all of the Future Children.
Does nothing if 'Restrict_ChildPairs' is disabled.
When enabled, pairings will be placed on a local location accessible as soon as the mother unit is accessible.
If disabled, the pairings will be found in the multiworld as any other item. Be warned, you require the pairings' item before the child's paralogue is accessible if enabled.
If 'Robin_PairPlus' is enabled, this option cannot place Robin's pair unless Robin is female. That's because the locations are females only.
Does nothing if 'Restrict_ChildPairs' is disabled.
Enables every Paralogue 18 to 23 which was obtained from SpotPass.
Does nothing if the Mad King is the goal.
Does nothing if 'Enable_Paralogues' option is disabled.
Adds an item for every Paralogue obtained from SpotPass.
Does nothing if the Mad King is the goal.
Adds Gangrel, Walhart, Emmeryn, Yen'fay, Aversa and Priam which are obtained from SpotPass.
Will not be added if the Mad King is the goal.
Adds every Bonus Team Character obtained from SpotPass.
These characters will be considered as Useful Items.
Only Exception is Marth which is required for his own class 'Lodestar' and as such need to be treated as progression.
When enabled every Main Chapter will require a 'Main Chapter Progression' of the same amount of its number before it is accessible.
If it is disabled, then each Main Chapter will have its own item called 'Main Chapter 1', 'Main Chapter 2' and so forth.
If enabled, will not restrict access to classes/skills that are reached by using Master or Second Seals.
Does nothing if related options are not enabled.
Useful for those who wish to farm Second/Master Seals from random merchants or Outrealm.
Otherwise the logic for Second Seals is being able to reach Chapter 16.
The Logic for reaching Master Seal is being able to reach Chapter 12.
You may have access to the seals earlier if Paralogues are enabled.
If you pick the Mad King as your goal this will be enabled by default.
If this option is enabled, you'll still require the Character-Specific Seals if they're enabled.
If enabled, will not treat the Avatar as no other class than Tactician and Grandmaster.
The same is applied for Morgan.
Useful for those who wish to experience more units when doing SkillSanity.
If enabled, will make Gaius be required to access chapter 6.
For those who wish to guarantee they can open chests early.
Note: Gaius or Anna is required for Chapter 11 and beyond as to not miss out on too much. They won't be required if the goal is the Mad King however.
If enabled, will make Chrom be required to access the Prologue Chapter.
For those who wish to have him from start.
Note: Chrom is required at the latest in Chapter 11 otherwise.
If enabled, will make Robin be required for Chapter 3.
For those who wish to have their Avatar early.
If enabled, will make Chrom, Robin, Lissa and Frederick be required to access Chapter 1.
For those who wish to guarantee those units early.
Note: You are already guaranteed Chrom, Robin or Frederick to be required for Chapter 3.
This option will try to make it so you have a certain amount of units before tackling specific chapters.
None: No logic for the amount of units you need for each chapter.
Full Restriction: You'll require the max amount of Units you can deploy before a Chapter is in logic starting with Chapter 5.
Medium Restriction: Chapter 5 will require 6 Units, Chapter 10 will require 10 units, Chapter 15 will require 12 units and Chapter 20 will require 14 units.
Low Restriction: Chapter 10 will require 5 units and Chapter 20 will require 10 Units.
It's an attempt to make sure you don't have to solo the whole game with just your starting unit.
NOTE: This option only restrict Main Chapters for now but may extend to Paralogues and Xenologues in the future.
If enabled, will add Anna, Say'ri, Flavia, Basilio and Tiki into the item pool.
Option is here for those that only wish to focus on the main cast and thus can disable them.
Reaching or Opening a chest in each chapter is a check.
Activating each event tile in each chapter is a check.
An event tile is a tile which sparkles on the map.
Buying Items from locations on the worldmap is a check.
These are accessible after chapter 4 to make sure you have some room to grind for gold if needed.
Defeating Enemies on each map is a check.
'Per Map' makes you defeat an x amount of enemies per map. Hard/Lunatic adds more to this count as they have increased enemies on each map.
'Per Type' will have you defeat each different enemy type you can find on a map. The only exception is Chapter 22 which will then label them by their names instead as they're all unique.
If the Mad King Goal is enabled, it may reduce the amount of enemies needed to be defeated in certain Xenologues.
Reaching certain levels for each Character is a check. Scales with which Main and Child Characters are enabled.
Base_Five: Reaching Level 5, 10, 15 and 20 in their Base Class is a check.
Promoted_Five: Reaching Level 5, 10, 15 and 20 in a Promoted Class is a check. This also includes 'Base_Five'.
Level_to_Twenty: Every level up to 20 from when you recruit them is a check.
Level_to_Max: Every level up to a promoted unit's level 20 is a check. This also includes 'Level_to_Twenty'.
NOTE: Taguel and Manakete Starting Units will max out their base class level at 20 even if 30 is their max level as leveling them up to max does nothing ingame.
NOTE: Units which start as a Promoted Unit does not have a Promoted Unit level requirement if 'Base_Five' is picked. They also do not gain any extra level up locations for Level_to_Max.

Disclaimer: There is a soft level cap for the locations in an attempt to not have you being forced to max level a unit as soon as it is unlocked in early game. This level cap should not be hard forced while playing the game.
For Base Classes: Level 5 requires Chapter 4, Level 10 requires chapter 8, Level 15 requires chapter 12 and Level 20 requires Chapter 14.
For Promoted Classes: Level 5 requires Chapter 14, Level 10 requires chapter 16, Level 15 requires chapter 18 and Level 20 requires Chapter 20.
NOTE: This soft level cap is reversed for Frederick as he is obtained early and is already Promoted.
Learning the various skills for Each Class is a check.
You won't need the actual skill as an item if you are using the 'Skills' option as you can still just unequip them if you don't have them unlocked.
Children's access to various classes are only restricted to their initial classes unless 'Restrict_ChildPairs' is enabled which will allow for a wider range of access.
NOTE: You may have to use Second Seals to reach skills from a Character's standard promoted classes as there is no good way to make sure you have access to all branches.
Every Support Rank between C to A for every main character is a check except S Rank as to not softlock anyone.
The Logic for reaching specific support ranks are as following; C requires Chapter 8, B requires chapter 10 and A requires chapter 12.
You may still reach the required support ranks earlier but this was the only way to not overwhelm you too early with the support grind!
Every Support Rank between C to A for every child character is a check except S Rank as to not softlock anyone.
This will include their parents but for the fathers it will not name one specifically and be more generic.
One of the only exceptions is Lucina which has Chrom as her guaranteed father and instead her mother will be labeled generic.
The other being Morgan which can have any combinations of Parents. If Male Robin is enabled, it will have a generic mother location and vice versa.
If Enabled, will add 3 locations for each Unit called 'Reached Support Rank C' and so forth instead of having every Support Convo as a location.
Does nothing if neither 'SupportSanity' or 'SupportSanity_Children' is enabled.
Every Village in each chapter is a check.
This also includes some NPCs that acts similar to Villages if the 'Enable Paralogues' option is enabled.
Saving Multiple NPCs for increased Rewards is a check.
This also includes letting Inigo get Kills for More Items in Inigo's Paralogue making him a requirement for his own Paralogue if this is enabled.
Also includes a few extra item checks here and there.
Items dropped by Enemies are a check. Those items which are highlighted in Green.
This does not include items obtained from recruitable enemies.
Items dropped by Enemy Reinforcements are a check. Those items which are highlighted in Green.
Items dropped by Enemies only on Lunatic difficulty are a check. Those items which are highlighted in Green.
When enabled every Xenologue(Outrealm Tale in EU) location will be available in the Multiworld.
Require any DLC to be enabled for their locations to be enabled though.
This option is here for those who just wish to use the other DLC Options without being forced to play through the DLCs as well.
When enabled every Xenologue(Outrealm Tale in EU) will require an item of its name before it is accessible.
When enabled together with the DLC the character is from, the dlc character will be added into the pool of characters you are allowed to use.
These characters will be considered as Useful Items.
Only Exception is Prince Marth which is required for his own class 'Lodestar' and as such need to be treated as progression.
When enabled together with the DLC the class is from, the dlc class will be added into the item pool.
Is only added if you have 'Base_Classes' enabled.
When enabled together with the DLC the skill is from, the dlc skill will be added into the item pool.
Is only added if you have 'Skills' enabled.
All the various DLC items will be added into the multiworld.
They are considered useful.
Requires the DLC they're from to be enabled or this option does nothing.
If enabled, will add the 'Wedding Bouqet' and 'Dread Scroll' into the multiworld.
These items are considered as progression and will be required before the respective classes are accessible.
Requires their DLC to be enabled or this option does nothing.
Enables Apotheosis's Secret Route locations.
Does nothing if the Apotheosis DLC is disabled.
Which Main Chapter do you wish to be the end point of your journey?
Mad King: The Playthrough goes all the way up to Chapter 11, requiring you to defeat the Mad King.
Grima: Require you to beat the final chapter.
None: All Main Chapters will still be included in the game but they may not be required to goal.
Some items, locations and characters will be disabled if the Mad King is the main goal.
When enabled requires you to beat 'Apothesis' in the Outrealm before you are able to goal.
Requires the Apothesis DLC to be enabled.
The goal will be accessible after you've reached Chapter 25 and have 20 eligble units.
Eligability is only checked if you have settings which restrict them and will not be able to make sure you have a balanced team.
For Child Characters, it will only check for classes outside their default classes unless 'Restrict_ChildPairs' is enabled as it won't know otherwise what classes are available to them.
It also checks if you have access to at least one weapon type for said classes if the Yaml Option is enabled.
This will only check if you have enough Main and Child Characters. Misc SpotPass and DLC Characters are not accounted for.
When enabled requires you to collect five 'Emblem Gemstones' for the Fire Emblem before you are able to goal.
These Gemstones are just macguffins, as soon as you have them in your inventory the goal will be accessible.
Five extra locations will also be added which requires each specific gemstone for it to be in logic.
When this is enabled, it will treat the list as a blacklist instead. Removing those pairs from the list of possible pairings.
NOTE! You need at least one Possible Pairing for each child or it won't go through generation.
Except for Lucina as if Chrom has no possible pairings he will always marry the Maiden.
Maiden will NEVER be randomly chosen and is merely a fallback if all his wives are manually taken already.
When this option is enabled, every Character except the Child Characters will be considered accessible from start.
You still require their respective items before they're in logic.
BE AWARE: This setting cannot guarantee you actually have access to them ingame, it's merely a way for people who can get later game characters earlier at any time with the aid of other means.

NOTE: If using Local_Pairs, you need access to their original Location before they're in logic as they are in the chapters' themselves. May be changed in the future, but if you intend to restrict_childpairs feel free to disable local pairs.
NOTE: Characters obtained past Chapter 11 remain unobtainable if the Mad King Goal is enabled.
When enabled will add a 'guidebook' for each group of classes that will be required before any of those classes are in logic.
The groups are based on their 'class trees' as can be found on Serenes Forest for the Class Introduction.
They're called 'How to be the Main Character', 'A Guide to Knighthood', 'Sword-wielding Guide', 'Guidebook for Fighters', 'How to Fly', 'Magic for Dummies' and 'Just be You'.
These are considered as Progression Items.
When enabled will add a 'key' for each location on the worldmap which prevents you from purchasing from them until found.
The name of the keys are the name of the location with 'Shop Key' added to it at the end.
These are considered as Progression Items.
NOTE: Paralogue Shop Keys will only be added if paralogues are enabled as well!
TIPS: I suggest allowing yourself to buy Bronze Weapons even if you do not have any keys for shops that sell them to prevent yourself from being forced to grind random encounters.
